National Assembly

Minutes of Proceedings

Volume 17 Ashad 2083
Wednesday
Meeting No. - 23

The National Assembly meeting commenced today at 13:20 hours under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson, Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members, names have been received to speak in the Zero Hour of today's National Assembly meeting. The proceedings will now commence. Honourable members, I have allocated 1 minute each for speaking in the Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Kamala Panta.

Honourable Mr. Kamala Panta (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, Honourable members raise issues of contemporary importance in this parliament many times. I don't think it's due to your unwillingness, Honourable Chairperson. I haven't heard you rule out any topics. What are the contemporary issues being raised in the parliament? What topics are being discussed in the Zero Hour, and what are the Honourable members drawing attention to? Despite this being the start of the session, it has been a long time, and I haven't seen the government address or respond to any of these issues. Therefore, I conclude my remarks by requesting the government's response to the issues raised concerning contemporary matters. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Jagat Bahadur Parki. Honourable Member Jagat Bahadur Parki. Honourable Member Jagat Bahadur Parki. Honourable Member Jayanti Devi Rai.

Honourable Ms. Jayanti Devi Rai (Communist Party of Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, due to three consecutive days of rainfall, a severe flood in the Sidhua River in Ward No. 1 of Silichong Rural Municipality, Sankhuwasabha district, has displaced 28 households. Furthermore, due to the disruption of electricity services, 600 households are currently in darkness and are staying with relatives. Although local security personnel and the local rural municipality have conducted some rescue operations, no relief materials have reached them. Therefore, through you, Honourable Chairperson, I wish to draw the serious attention of the government to this matter and urge the government to immediately provide relief materials and arrange for their safe resettlement. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Durga Gurung.

Honourable Mr. Durga Gurung (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, I wish to draw the serious attention of the government. The incident involving 28-year-old Dambar Tamang, who was displaced during the eviction of landless squatters and disorganized settlements and is currently staying at a holding center in Kirtipur, has raised serious humanitarian and legal questions. It has been reported that he was arrested while expressing his suffering amidst displacement, poor health, uncertain livelihood, and mental stress. If any citizen has to face legal proceedings or unjust treatment simply for expressing their pain, it is not in accordance with the democratic governance system and the spirit of the constitution. I urge the Government of Nepal that the incident (...time expired.)

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Nar Bahadur Bisht.

Honourable Mr. Nar Bahadur Bisht (Communist Party of Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, through you, Honourable Chairperson, the government has not yet responded to the issues raised by Honourable members during the Zero Hour and Special Time. The government, formed in the name of good governance and transparency, has not taken any responsibility for the issues raised by the people's representatives in the parliament, and we have not received any answers so far. Therefore, I wish to draw the attention of the Right Honourable Chairperson to when the answers to the questions raised so far will be provided, and whether it is busy with good governance? Is the government busy with transparency? Where is this transparency and good governance? If the government does not respond to the pressing daily issues raised here, then...

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar.

Honourable Mr. Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar (Communist Party of Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, they say good governance is the main agenda of this government. Seven billion rupees worth of vehicles are burning inside Singha Durbar, and directives are being issued to purchase three billion rupees worth of vehicles for development construction. Hundreds of thousands of squatters are being driven to holding centers. During this rainy season, 24,000 people are being driven out, saying they cannot stay in the holding centers. The condition of the visually impaired is also the same. Disorder has been created in education. There are discussions that 35,000 minors under 18 years of age have been made party members. Does this government not have to follow the constitution? Does the law not apply to this government? Is this good governance? Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Mohammad Khalid.

Honourable Mr. Mohammad Khalid (Janata Samajwadi Party, Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, the news that 127 Nepali citizens have died so far among those who joined the Russian army out of compulsion due to poverty and unemployment is extremely sad and worrying. I express my condolences to the families of the deceased. There is also information that about 100 Nepalis are missing. How many Nepalis have gone to Russia and Ukraine so far? It is necessary to collect accurate data and rescue them. I thank the Honourable Minister of Foreign Affairs for his initiative in this regard. However, such incidents will not stop solely through diplomatic initiatives. Therefore, I request that opportunities be created within the country and an environment of hope and trust for employment within the country be established. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire.

Honourable Ms. Rajendra Laxmi Gaire (Communist Party of Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, the new government formed with the support of the Gen Z, a government with a two-thirds majority. We had many expectations. The Nepali people had expectations. But day after day, numerous incidents are being reported. Just recently, Santoshi Shrestha, a 28-year-old student from Bharatpur Nursing College, left on her scooter and her scooter was found near the Devghat temple three days ago. We still don't know where that daughter is today. There is also the Supa Deurali incident. Why are our daughters disappearing in broad daylight today? This is a serious question. Another issue is that last year, teachers protested for 19 days, and their demands were not met (...time expired.)

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Yuvraj Sharma.

Honourable Mr. Yuvraj Sharma (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, more than 200,000 children between the ages of one and five years are suffering from malnutrition. I want to ask if the leaders and ministers of Rastriya Swatantra Party, who consumed eight quintals of meat at their general convention, remembered the faces of these children. In the month of Chaitra, chicken farmers have not received compensation for the loss of lakhs of chickens that died due to bird flu. The government appears slow in this regard. Now, even the residents of Sustaa have come to Kathmandu. Should the Honourable Prime Minister call them encroachers or the encroached upon? Should they be called Nepali or others? Is this influenced by some Madhesi language translated into Hindi films? A bill related to time-bound transport and traffic with a strict penalty is being introduced. This needs to be corrected. Because the country does not run on films and film dialogues, nor on applause and criticism. The government should be freed from such handover as soon as possible (...time expired.)

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar.

Honourable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Communist Party of Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, as soon as this government came to power, it forcibly evicted squatters from various squatter settlements using force and kept them in various holding centers in a state of distress. Now, again, without any guarantee of a safe place and without such arrangements, they are being evicted from the holding centers as well, reportedly for a small amount of money. It is heard that they are saying they cannot keep many people here. If they could not make proper arrangements in the holding centers, if they could not arrange safe places for them within that short period, then they should have thought about it at that time? At that time, they should have thought carefully and considered other options for the squatters, shouldn't they? I wish to draw the government's attention to this matter of evicting them without any reason. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members, the Zero Hour speaking order concludes here. Honourable members, the National Assembly directs all the Honourable Ministers of the Government of Nepal.

Honourable members, a letter regarding the assignment of responsibilities of the Council of Ministers has been received from the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers. I will now provide information about the contents of that letter.

It is requested that Honourable Minister of Agriculture, Forest and Environment, Gita Chaudhary, who left for Bangkok, Thailand on Ashad 14, 2083, to participate in the "nineth session of the committee on environment and development and the ministerial level" program related to the Paris Agreement and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, will have her responsibilities in the Ministry of Agriculture, Forest and Environment handled by the Honourable Minister of Communications and Information Technology, Dr. Vikram Timilsina, during her absence.

Suman Raj Aryal,
Chief Secretary
Ashad 14, 2083

Honourable members, after the Honourable Minister responds, if the questioner Honourable member wishes, they will be able to ask a supplementary question related to their topic within 1 minute. Honourable members, I request the Honourable Minister of Foreign Affairs, Shishir Khanal, to come to the rostrum to answer the questions posed by the Honourable members.

Honourable Minister of Foreign Affairs Mr. Shishir Khanal: Honourable Chairperson, Honourable...

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable member, now I provide time to the questioner Honourable Member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar to ask his question.

Honourable Mr. Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar (Communist Party of Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, through you, Honourable Chairperson, my question to the Honourable Minister is as follows: It was publicly reported that there is a large deposit of uranium ore in the Mustang district of Nepal and that the Nepali Army and the US Army have agreed to its excavation. What is the reality of this? I would like to ask the Honourable Minister. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Minister.

Honourable Minister of Foreign Affairs Mr. Shishir Khanal: Honourable Chairperson, Honourable member, I wish to inform you that there is no truth to the public discussion about an agreement between the Nepali Army and the US Army for the excavation of uranium ore in Mustang district. No agreement or understanding has been reached with anyone regarding mining in this region. Relevant bodies of the Government of Nepal have also refuted the baseless claims made by some digital media in this regard. The government is fully committed to the provisions regarding natural resources and their utilization as per Article 279 of the Constitution of Nepal, 2072. I also wish to clarify that Nepal will not enter into any agreements contrary to the principles of its non-aligned foreign policy and policies. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member, the questioner Honorable Member wishes to ask a supplementary question, so I am providing time to ask a supplementary question focused on the topic. (13:36 PM) Honorable Mr. Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar (Communist Party of Nepal):- Honorable Chairperson, is it true that there is uranium metal in Mustad? If so, what plan has the government made for its conservation, exploration, and promotion? What is the current situation? Thank you. Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Minister. (13:36 PM) Honorable Minister of Foreign Affairs Mr. Shishir Khanal:- Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Member, preliminary studies indicate the possibility of mining in Mustad. However, further study and exploration are needed. The Department of Mines of Nepal will take necessary steps in this regard. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Members, I now provide time for the questioner Honorable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma to ask his question. (13:37 PM) Honorable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Communist Party of Nepal):- Honorable Chairperson, through you, Honorable Chairperson, I wish to ask the Honorable Minister the following question: Why and for how long has the construction work of the embankment being built on the Narayani River in Susta Rural Municipality, West Nawalparasi, been stopped due to the intervention of the Indian SSB? What administrative, security, and diplomatic initiatives has the Government of Nepal taken so far to end Indian interference in the construction of Nepali land and development in Susta? What is the government's clear plan for the long-term solution of the border dispute? I also demand clarification. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Minister. (13:38 PM) Honorable Minister of Foreign Affairs Mr. Shishir Khanal:- Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Member, it is well known that Nepal and India have a centuries-old long and open border. Nepal's current international border is primarily established and directed by the Treaty of Sugauli of 1816. The demarcation of the Nepal-India border is yet to be completed in the Susta and Limpiyadhura, Lipulek, and Kalapani areas. In this context, on 2083/2/17, a joint team of Nepal's Armed Police Force and India's SSB, during border monitoring along the Nepal-India border in Susta Rural Municipality 5, Susta, West Nawalparasi district on the Nepali side and Rampurwa, West Champaran district on the Indian side, observed that regarding the construction of approximately 1 kilometer of embankment with an endpoint approximately 250 meters west of the Nepal-India border in Nepali territory in Susta Rural Municipality 5, the Indian side has no objection to the construction work. It is understood that the Indian side has requested that construction work proceed only after necessary coordination between the relevant officials of both countries before further new construction work of 132 meters of embankment by the Irrigation and Water Resource Management Project, Bharatpur, Chitwan, on the eastern side of the embankment within Nepali territory. The border management is continuously carried out through meetings of the Nepal-India border-related bilateral mechanism "Joint Working Group" and its sub-mechanisms. Nepal's Armed Police Force and India's Border Security Force are working in coordination in the border areas. The Government of Nepal is always committed to resolving border-related issues through diplomatic dialogue in accordance with the spirit and intention of historical treaties, agreements, and maps between Nepal and India. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Members, the questioner Honorable Member wishes to ask a supplementary question, so I am providing time to ask a supplementary question focused on the topic. (13:41 PM) Honorable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Communist Party of Nepal):- Honorable Chairperson, through you, Honorable Chairperson, I wish to ask the Honorable Minister a supplementary question: a new issue has arisen. I want to clarify: is it true that the borders of Susta, Limpiyadhura, Lipulek, and Kalapani have not been demarcated? If so, the record of the then headman of the Bat area, Kuti, Kunji, Nabhi, and Tidar areas, Harikrishna Buda, paying land revenue to the Darchula Land Revenue Office in 1985 BS is still fresh. Voting took place in the general elections of 2015 BS, and national census was conducted by a team led by Bhairav Bahadur Gantawa in 2018 BS, which is also fresh. Although the previous governments have not dared to do so. According to the Treaty of Sugauli, the territory east of the Mahakali River is an integral part of Nepal. Our current map of Nepal is also fresh. Furthermore, one country obstructing the development work of another country is sheer arrogance. Diplomatic initiatives should be sought from the government. When will the embankment construction work resume? Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Minister. (13:42 PM) Honorable Minister of Foreign Affairs Mr. Shishir Khanal:- Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Member, I have informed the esteemed house before. The bilateral technical committee between Nepal and India has demarcated the borders in many areas of Nepal and India. However, it is true that the bilateral technical team has not demarcated the borders in the Limpiyadhura, Lipulek, Kalapani areas, and Susta area. That is the truth, that is a fact. But let us be clear, those territories belong to Nepal. We have historical bases, evidence, and maps, and based on those, I have informed the esteemed house before. I have also stated this when I met my Indian counterpart: it is natural for neighbors to have some differences and disputes, but I want to resolve this dispute through diplomatic dialogue based on historical facts and evidence. In that sense, this fact is true. It is a fact that the borders have not been formally demarcated by both sides in Kalapani, Limpiyadhura, Lipulek, and Susta areas, but we need to move forward with this, and we are working to resolve this issue through diplomatic dialogue. Apart from this, in areas other than these two main areas, the technical committee related to border measurement is still working today, and we want to move these tasks forward continuously through the bilateral mechanisms we have. Similarly, we are trying to move forward with the embankment issue through diplomatic dialogue and mutual understanding between the two countries. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Members, the Honorable Minister of Foreign Affairs has requested time to speak on a current issue. I now provide him time to speak on a current issue. (13:44 PM) Honorable Minister of Foreign Affairs Mr. Shishir Khanal:- Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Members, I have been informing this esteemed house from time to time about the work carried out by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and most recently, I addressed this house on Jestha 28, 2083 BS. I wish to reiterate that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which I lead, is continuously working to promote national interest and the country's image by protecting Nepal's sovereignty, territorial integrity, national independence, and autonomy, and the security and rights of Nepali citizens, while prioritizing good governance and economic prosperity in line with Nepal's constitution, foreign policy, and established principles of international relations. I wish to inform this esteemed house about my recently concluded visit to China and various issues related to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs raised by Honorable Members in this house. I have concluded a four-day official visit to China from Jestha 31 to Ashar 3, 2083 BS, corresponding to June 14 to 17, 2026, at the friendly invitation of His Excellency Mr. Wang Yi, Member of the Political Bureau of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China. During the visit, on June 15, 2026, I held a bilateral meeting with His Excellency Mr. Wang Yi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China, in Beijing. On that occasion, both delegations held in-depth and fruitful discussions on all aspects of Nepal-China bilateral relations. There was consensus between both sides on further strengthening Nepal-China relations based on mutual friendship, goodwill, and cooperation. Reaffirming the Nepali government's commitment to the One China principle, it was clearly stated that Nepal's territory would not be used against China's interests. Similarly, the Chinese side reiterated its firm support for Nepal's sovereignty, territorial integrity, and independence and expressed confidence in the Nepali government's priorities in the areas of good governance and economic development. Reaffirming mutual respect and commitment to each other's priorities and sensitivities, discussions were held on expanding cooperation in various fields, including infrastructure, connectivity, border management, energy, trade, investment, agricultural technology transfer, information technology and digitalization, tourism, chemical fertilizers, exploration of petroleum and natural gas, and people-to-people relations. Similarly, commitment was expressed to the early implementation of bilateral programs and projects agreed upon in the past, and emphasis was placed on advancing cooperation on issues of common interest in multilateral and regional forums. Prior to the meeting, I met with His Excellency Mr. Liu Haixing, Minister of the International Department of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (IDCPC) of the People's Republic of China. On that occasion, ideas were exchanged on further strengthening Nepal-China relations and expanding bilateral cooperation. Similarly, on June 16, 2026, I met with His Excellency Mr. Wang Huning, Chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference of the People's Republic of China. On that occasion, discussions were held on further strengthening the cordial, friendly, and cooperative relations between Nepal and China and enhancing cooperation in priority areas. Similarly, I participated in an Investment Conference organized by the Nepali Embassy in Beijing with the aim of promoting Chinese investment in Nepal. I had fruitful meetings with Chinese businessmen, entrepreneurs, and investors. On that occasion, a presentation was made by representatives of the Investment Board Nepal on "Invest in Nepal: Opportunities, Incentives, and Partnership Prospects," and detailed interaction took place among the participants. Addressing the program, I called upon Chinese investors to invest in Nepal and build a new chapter of prosperity along with mutual economic growth. I informed them about Nepal's existing economic potential and demographic strength and assured them that the Government of Nepal is committed to creating an investment and business-friendly environment. During the visit, I also met and interacted with representatives of the Nepali community in China by participating in a reception hosted by the Nepali Embassy in Beijing. Informing them about the Government of Nepal's priorities of institutionalizing good governance, economic development, and prosperity, I also urged them to actively participate in the campaign of nation-building.

I have called. Similarly, I have informed about the work of the embassy and instructed the officials there to strengthen Nepal-China relations, conduct economic and development diplomacy effectively, and protect the interests of Nepalis in China and provide effective services. Also, in separate meetings with Nepali, Chinese, and international media organized at the embassy, I have expressed my views on Nepal's foreign policy, Nepal-China relations, the priorities of the newly formed Nepal government, and Nepal's engagement with the international community. During the visit, I observed the Shesh Stupa at the Swayambhu Temple in Beijing. This cultural heritage, designed by the national luminary Arniko of Nepal, stands as a symbol of the multifaceted cultural and people-to-people relations between Nepal and China. It also serves as an example of the international recognition of Nepali artisans and Nepali architecture. Similarly, I visited the Institute of Tibetan Plateau Research at the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) in Beijing and learned about the activities of the institute and its collaboration with Tribhuvan University and other Nepali institutions. In interactions with senior officials of the institute, I emphasized the need to deepen and make the cooperation between Nepal and China in the field of science and technology more fruitful. I also visited the first high-tech and national innovation demonstration zone in Beijing, the Science Park, and learned about its activities and priorities. My participation in meetings with the Foreign Minister and high-ranking officials of the People's Republic of China during my visit to China, as well as other programs, has made a significant contribution to further strengthening the friendly and multifaceted Nepal-China relations and expanding and consolidating cooperation on issues of mutual interest. Furthermore, this visit has been of significant help in achieving the Nepal government's objective of expanding independent, pragmatic, and cooperative relations with all countries, including neighbors, and promoting economic and development diplomacy. Now, I would like to provide information regarding various issues related to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs raised by the honorable members. The issue raised by Honorable Ms. Samjhana Devkota regarding opening the Nepal-China border crossings and upgrading them to facilitate arrivals is a priority for the government. Currently, three international crossings (Hilsa, Pulang-Purang, Rasuwagadhi-Kerung, and Kodari-Zhangmu) and three bilateral crossings (Lizi-Nechung, Korala-Mustang, and Kimathanka-Chentang, Olangchunggola, Rasuwa) and other traditional crossings are operational between Nepal and the People's Republic of China. This matter is also facilitated through coordination between the local administrations of Nepal and China. I have requested that initiatives be taken to open or determine the modality of operation of the border crossings through discussions and consultations with the Chinese side through the said levels and mechanisms, as per the need and bilateral understanding. I also discussed this matter further with my counterpart during my visit to China to better manage the border crossings between the two countries. Similarly, the issue of tea export from Nepal was also raised. The government is continuously working to address and resolve the problems seen in the export of Nepali tea to India, as the honorable house is aware. In this regard, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Nepali Embassy in India are continuously engaged in diplomatic efforts through dialogue with high-ranking officials from India's Ministry of External Affairs, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Food Safety and Standards Authority, and the Indian Tea Board. Discussions were also held at the high-level during my visit to India in May. As a result, I would like to inform you that this problem has now been resolved, and the export of Nepali tea to India has become easier. Just a few days ago, India facilitated our exports by making some modifications to its policy. Similarly, regarding the issue of helicopter entry into the Darcula district raised by Honorable Mr. Roshni Mechhe, according to the information received from the relevant bodies, it has not been observed that an Indian helicopter entered Nepali territory with intent or malicious intent, and contact and coordination are ongoing between Nepali officials and the Indian side regarding the entry into Nepali territory due to the geographical location and weather of that area. Honorable Mr. Somnath Poudel has inquired about the export of betel nut. We are aware of this matter and are coordinating with the relevant bodies. Similarly, about 1.8 million Nepalis are working in the West Asian region. A question was asked about the data of Nepalis displaced due to the Iran war. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is fully sensitive and committed to the security, protection, interests, and welfare of Nepalis working in the West Asian region, especially in the context of the Iran war. During the America-Israel-Iran conflict in West Asia, I want to ensure the necessary work for the security, interests, and welfare of Nepali citizens in trouble in that region. With the coordination of diplomatic missions in that region, some Nepalis stranded in transit were repatriated to Nepal or sent to their destinations. Although some Nepalis returned to their home country due to family personal reasons or the fear of the situation worsening during the conflict, it is informed to the honorable house that a significant number of Nepalis have not been displaced due to the conflict. This can also be assessed from the pressure received at that time to open labor permits and re-labor permits. It is also informed to the honorable house that the situation there is normalizing. Similarly, a question was raised regarding LDC graduation. There are various reasons why Nepal needs to postpone or defer its LDC graduation. Among them are the various economic fluctuations Nepal has faced since the past, the Russia-Ukraine war, increasing climate change-induced disaster risks, high poverty rates, low productivity, weak competitive capacity, weak export base, damages from the movement on August 29 and 30, 2082, and the impact on Nepal's economic and social sectors, as well as the conflict in the Middle East. Considering these factors, the decision has been made to postpone Nepal's graduation from Least Developed Country status, which was scheduled for November 24, 2026, and to extend the graduation period by an additional three years. I wish to inform the honorable house that a request has been made to the relevant bodies of the United Nations on May 13, 2026, for this purpose. Similarly, a question was raised regarding passports. Given the close and cooperative relationship between Nepal and Germany, meetings and dialogues are natural. In this context, there is no truth to the claim that the acting ambassador of the Nepali Embassy in Berlin gave a rude response to an official from the German Foreign Ministry. The meeting was cordial, like other meetings. During the meeting with the acting ambassador, it is natural to show interest in companies from one's own country. During the meeting, the acting ambassador informed that the issue related to passport procurement is currently sub-judice in the judicial body, and its resolution will be in accordance with Nepal's laws. Similarly, the issue of the Gauriphanta border crossing as an international border crossing was also raised. The Gauriphanta border crossing in Kailali is operational, and upgrading this border crossing is also on the agenda of the intergovernmental mechanism meeting between Nepal and India. I wish to inform the honorable house that this agenda has been raised at various times and levels, and efforts will continue. Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Members, we are working with a focus on foreign policy and international relations centered on national interest and the country's image. Our main objective is to work with national interest at the center. As the management of foreign relations is a sensitive matter, we all have a responsibility, contribution, and role in this regard. In conclusion, I reiterate my commitment that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has been performing strong and effective work within its jurisdiction and will continue to do so in the future, and will keep this honorable house informed of the achievements made. I also seek the guidance of the honorable members. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Members, I would like to invite the Honorable Minister of Culture, Tourism, and Civil Aviation, Khadak Raj Paudel, to the rostrum to answer the questions posed by the honorable members. Honorable Members, I will now provide time to the questioner Honorable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma to ask his question. Honorable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Nepali Communist Party): Honorable Chairperson, through you, I would like to ask the Honorable Minister: regarding the Sunathali Airport in Kalikot, which started construction in 2042 BS, with an investment of over 42 crore rupees, and was formally inaugurated on Falgun 14, 2080 BS, what concrete steps are being taken by the Civil Aviation Authority and other bodies to address the actual progress, obstacles in operation, and to resume regular flights, and by when is regular service expected to commence? I demand clarification. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Minister. Honorable Minister of Culture, Tourism, and Civil Aviation, Mr. Khadak Raj Paudel: Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Members, Questioner Honorable Member, regarding the Sunathali Airport in Kalikot, the construction of the unpaved runway has been completed, and the first test flight was successfully conducted on Magh 29, 2073 BS, corresponding to February 11, 2017, with a Twin Otter aircraft of Tara Air. Subsequently, the blacktopping of the runway was completed in the fiscal year 2079/080, and a second successful test flight was conducted on Falgun 13, 2080 BS, again with a Twin Otter aircraft of Tara Air. As per the flight schedule approved by the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal, Nepal Airlines has obtained permission to operate flights on the Surkhet-Kalikot-Surkhet route every Tuesday and Saturday. However, regular flights have not been able to operate at this airport mainly due to the lack of passenger volume, or in common parlance, the availability of passengers. To commence regular flight operations at this airport, discussions were held at the initiative of the Authority with Nepal Airlines, Tara Air, Summit Air, Sita Air, and representatives from Kalikot. Although Tara Air agreed to operate flights twice a week, the local representatives, with whom discussions were held, could not guarantee passenger numbers, and therefore, regular scheduled flights have not been possible to date. In the coming days, if the necessary coordination between the local level and the airline operators leads to the assurance of regular passengers, the Government of Nepal and the Civil Aviation Authority are committed to providing the necessary technical manpower, ATC, communication equipment, and other technical arrangements. The commitment letter from the Civil Aviation Authority was received on Jestha 19, 2083, under reference number 39. I wish to inform the honorable house. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson:- Now, the honorable member will be given time to ask follow-up questions on the subject. (14:04 hrs) Honorable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Nepal Communist Party):- Honorable Chairperson Sir, through you, I would like to ask the honorable minister a follow-up question. The Sunathali Airport is remembered for this reason: on February 11, 2058 BS, during the daytime, the contractor Kumar Thapa, along with 30 laborers from Dhading, Jogimara, and Ramechhap, Dolakha, and 6 laborers from Kalikot, totaling 36 laborers, were massacred by the Nepali Army and buried in a single mass grave. The claim that there is no certainty of passengers is false. This should not mislead the government either. The truth is that there is no lack of passengers, but the authority did not send technicians. Even though the rural municipality agreed to bear the cost for a temporary vacant seat, why were technicians not sent? This is a tragedy. And through the Honorable Chairperson, the people of Kalikot district want to ask the Honorable Minister: the people of Kalikot have asked, in which month, on which date, and at what time will the Sunathali Airport have its next landing? Thank you. Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Minister. (14:05 hrs) Honorable Minister of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation, Mr. Khadga Raj Poudel:- Honorable Chairperson, I thank you for informing the house about the tragic history of Sunathali Airport. No matter how difficult or tragic the history, the biggest problem among the problems of airport operation in Nepal is the lack of passenger numbers. In total, there are 54 airports, of which 34 are operational. 21 are non-operational, and most of the reports we receive from mountain region airports cite the lack of passenger numbers as the primary reason. The main reasons for this are migration and the increasing availability of roads in villages, and road transport being slightly cheaper than air travel. We have been informed that this is why passenger numbers are low. According to the response from the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal, if technicians are needed and there is a minimum availability of passengers for regular flights, we will definitely send technical manpower and equipment. We have no shortage of equipment and manpower in the CAAN, but rather than sending them to places that are not operational and keeping them idle, we are sending them to operational places. This has also been included in the upcoming fiscal budget for more effective implementation. The Ministry has been providing support to safe shelters operating in 21 local levels for women affected by gender-based violence, and two long-term rehabilitation centers are in operation, including one at Kendra Mangala Sahana. For victims of gender-based violence, a communication system has been established for psychosocial counseling and other services. The speaker emphasized the need for new laws, curriculum integration, and targeted programs to combat digital violence, including cyberbullying, stalking, and deepfakes.
